narrative:
The 2018 Pittsburgh Pirates opened the year with a jolt of drama on the very first day of the season, surrendering a crushing two-run double before Gregory Polanco answered with a three-run blast that set the tone for what would be a season of wild swings. April proved fruitful, as the Pirates rode clutch moments — Corey Dickerson's reviewed-and-upheld homer, Jordy Mercer's walk-off double, and Starling Marte's timely single — to a 16-12 mark that kept the club firmly in contention.

May and June told a different story. The bullpen, particularly Felipe Vázquez and George Kontos, struggled to hold late leads, and opponents repeatedly feasted on Pittsburgh's relievers in high-leverage situations. The Pirates finished May at 12-15 and June at 10-16, tumbling out of playoff position as the Cardinals, Brewers, and others drove dagger after dagger through their rotation and pen. Colin Moran's two-run homer on May 9 offered a brief lift, but those bright moments were overwhelmed by a tide of blown opportunities.

July was the season's turning point and its most brilliant chapter. The Pirates surged to a 17-9 record — their best month — fueled by an extraordinary comeback against the Brewers on July 15 that featured a David Freese triple and Josh Bell's game-winning double, one of the highest-leverage plays of the entire year. Colin Moran's grand slam on July 1 had already signaled this club could win big games when it needed to.

The final two months were a tale of two halves in miniature. August collapsed to 10-17 as the bullpen again failed in critical moments, and a brutal Clay Holmes outing against Milwaukee on August 24 encapsulated the frustration. But September saw the Pirates reignite, going 16-10 and finishing on the right side of .500 at 82-79. Jacob Stallings, Starling Marte, and others delivered late-season heroics that gave the fanbase something to remember — even if it was not quite enough to punch a ticket to October.

chapters.title: Opening Day Fireworks
chapters.description: The Pirates open the season with immediate high drama, surrendering big hits before Polanco's three-run homer swings the momentum back.

chapters.title: April Surge
chapters.description: Pittsburgh rides clutch performances from Mercer, Marte, and Dickerson to a winning April and a foothold in the playoff race.

chapters.title: Bullpen Blues
chapters.description: May and June unravel as the Pirates' relievers repeatedly surrender leads in high-leverage moments, sending the team into a steep slide.

chapters.title: July Resurrection
chapters.description: The Pirates go 17-9 in their best month, capped by a stunning Brewers comeback featuring Freese, Bell, and Moran delivering when it mattered most.

chapters.title: August Fade
chapters.description: The bullpen implodes again in August, with Clay Holmes and others surrendering critical late-game leads that doom Pittsburgh's playoff hopes.

chapters.title: September Pride
chapters.description: With the playoffs out of reach, the Pirates play their best baseball of the second half, going 16-10 on the strength of Marte, Stallings, and a revived lineup.
